text_fidelity_a: Neo Nautical Sundial Compass George Australia Sundial Watch Camping Hiking It’s a beautiful compass and the case is nice. I saw other reviews that said east and west were mixed up on their compasses. When you look at this compass, the painted end of the needle will point towards N on the rose when you’re facing N and it will point to S on the rose when facing S. However, the painted end of the needle will point towards W on the rose when you’re facing E and it will point to E in the rose when you’re facing W. As this isn’t an orienteering compass there’s nothing for you to adjust so that it shows the direction of travel. Just remember that the needle will always point north and if you remember where east, south and west are in regards to north then you will know which direction you’re truly facing.

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman 100 Quart Xtreme 5 Wheeled Cooler Having owned one of these for a few years I feel more than qualified to review this.

- To the people who say it doesn't work, first "temper" the cooler. That means you bring it inside, put cold items in it and let it sit. I temper mine for several days before use.
- Second, use block ice. I use the square ice cream containers from Wally-World. They pack nicely, stack nicely and are easy for me to get in my freezer to make the blocks. Barring that, keep the ice you guy in bags. The greater the ice mass, the less quickly it melts. I also use water bottles filled close to the top. I'll freeze them, cap them after they're frozen and put them in the cooler. You've a double use: ice and cold water when it melts.
- Third, make sure the products you put in the cooler start out cold. Again, the colder they are, the longer they'll stay cold.
- Fourth, don't expect anything in direct sunlight or on hot ground to stay cold. If you need, park this on a couple blocks of wood to get it off the ground and get air flow under it. Hot ground will eventually cause the cooler to become hot. Insulation doesn't care whether it's keeping cold things cold or hot things hot. If you get it hot, it'll start making things inside hot.
- Lastly, if you have water and still have ice, that COLD water makes a good conductor of cool temperatures. If you drain the water you're not doing yourself a favor. You should have your foods in ziplock bags for best protection.

I've used this cooler on an extended trip to the Sequoias from Eastern Washington State. This rode in the back of my pick up with only a tarp for shade. The trip south took three days (owing to stops at family and friends). No additional ice required. Once at the campground, still no ice required.
We were at the campground a week. After that week we did drain off excess and add more ice. The return trip was through Lake Tahoe on to Nevada, staying at Carson City for three days, over to Oregon - staying in Ontario, OR and then back home. Yup, most of the ice had melted, but the larger pieces kept the water cold.

If you take care of your cooler, it should take care of you. The handle is nice and wide with an easy grip. The wheels move nicely and everything feels comfortable when pulling it along.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman 100 Quart Xtreme 5 Wheeled Cooler

text_fidelity_a: Under Armour Elevate 22 Ounce Tritan Bottle with Flip Top Lid I ordered four of these in 2015 0r 2016. Over time, I have lost a couple and/or left them on the roof of my car and pulled off. :-D I just ordered four more. I'm VERY picky about water bottles. I expect them to be easy to fill with both ice of any size and, of course, liquids. I expect them to fit easily and well into auto cup holders. I expect the spout that touches my lips to be thin for easy drinking. I expect to be able to put them in the freezer half filled with water to make an ice base for my drinks. I expect them to be lightweight, even when filled. This is the only water bottle I've ever owned that meets all of my expectations. No, it is not insulted, and yes, it does "sweat" sometimes. But I live in Las Vegas, so I use these CONSTANTLY. I've never had any problems with leaking, breaking, or anything else, and since I'm a community college prof, I put these through some pretty heavy use between carting them in backpacks, totes, and luggage and knocking them off desks. text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Folding Standard Weight Bench – Easy Storage MWB-20100, Incline I ordered this weight bench (March MWB-20100 Standard Bench) for my teenager and he loves it. I will first give you his comments and then end the review by giving my own.

A 14-year-old’s honest review:

In high school, I take weight training for PE. I have learned a lot but thought that some equipment at home would really help. So when my mom got this one, I was excited. This weight bench was very easy to put together. And because I couldn’t wait, I put it together myself instead of waiting for my father to get home. All I had to do was match the numbers to the pictures and the only tool I needed was a wrench. It was easy to assemble, only took me about 30 minutes to put together and I’m only 14. Don’t worry my dad did check my work when he got home. You can do a few different things with this bench. You can do the standard lifts or arm/bicep curls. I am 6’2, 159lbs and have really long arms, so it is a little close but is fine for me to use. By close, I am talking about the weight hooks. They are closer than the ones on the equipment I use at school. I also like that you can adjust the seats and back on the bench. This is great for when you work certain areas of the body. The cushions are comfortable and well padded with foam. Beware that this bench does not come with the bar or weights, but I had my mom to go to the local sports store and order some. I got a decent set for under $200. Regardless, I like this bench a lot. It allows me to build a little muscle without having to go to the gym at school. I deducted half a star for the closeness of the hooks.

Now what “mom” likes about this bench:

I liked the fact that he could put this together himself (I’m directionally challenged and his dad wasn’t at home), with very few tools. It occupies some of his time and gives him a productive outlet for teenage frustration and angst (smile). He can close himself in the room, play his music and pump away. And if I am so moved and want a light workout, this set isn’t so overwhelming or complicated that I am too intimidated to use it. BUT THE FEATURE THAT I LOVE AND THE ONE I THINK ALL MOMS WILL LOVE is the fact that by removing one of the pins, you can fold it vertically and it takes up little space. Meaning if you don’t have a basement, and I don’t….and choose to dedicate one room to exercise equipment, you won’t be overwhelmed by the size of it all. I have this bench in my extra bedroom, which is also a computer room. When company comes, or when I want to use the space for something else, I can release, pull up and store it. How fantastic is that?

And finally, as a consumer, this bench appears to be comparably priced with others on the market. When I priced bars and weights, I noticed that the local sports stores were selling the Marcy brand for comparably what Amazon was charging. Marcy is a brand known in the exercise equipment arena. The product appears to be well made and durable. For amateurs and young teens, this would be a decent purchase at under $250. I highly recommend it and give it 4.5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Folding Standard Weight Bench – Easy Storage MWB-20100, Incline

SABRE Ruger Tactical Model with Pepper Spray & Practice Spray, Black We have mountain lions and coyote where we live. It's not a bad idea to carry some spray when going on hikes. Especially if you're by yourself.

So this seemed like it might fit the bill. The case seems simple enough, but it had a lot of parts. Parts that could easily get lost. There's a little retainer clip for the thumb trigger that I accidentally popped off with my thumb a few times. There's the cannister retainer clip that is indexed so you can only install it one way. There's a semi clear plug that drops out of the bottom if you decide to switch the belt clip side. So I'd like to see a simplified version of the case.

Loading and unloading is fairly simple. Pull the cannister clip. Lift the trigger clip and thumb trigger and pull out the old cannister and drop in the new one.

Deploying the spray is a simple point at target, insert thumb and press the thumb trigger. The range is not great, but might be enough to make the difference between harm and escape.

I've had some experience CS gas training and had considered trying out some of the spray, but decided against it. Like a fire extinguisher, I'm just going to assume that it works as described.

Also, made in the USA.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Ruger Tactical Model with Pepper Spray & Practice Spray, Black

PCKL Premium Pickleball Paddle Racket | USA Pickleball Approved | Graphite Carbon Face with Large Sweet Spot | Honeycomb Core Love this paddle! This is my first paddle, as I am a pickleball newbie. For context, I've been playing ~8 hours per week for the past couple months. After using the wooden paddles for a few weeks, I decided to get my own.

This paddle is absolutely my favorite of any of the paddles I've tried, (and I tried paddles of all shapes, sizes, weights, etc). The elongated shape is helpful when reaching for balls and slamming, although the sweet spot is a little smaller than on a wide-body or standard paddle. The slightly smaller sweet spot has not affected my play.

The face of this PCKL paddle is a textured graphite and it makes a very satisfying sound/feel when you hit the ball just right. The paddle is also on the lighter side (weighing ~7.5 oz), which allows me to hit to ball a little harder without it going way out of bounds.

Lastly, I really like the look and design of the paddle. The white/green look is very clean, and the green outline around the face helps you easily spot it when in a stack of paddles (at a pickup court).

I have 2 gripes, both very minor. One is that the length of the handle is a *tiny* bit short for my liking--another few centimeters would have been perfect (that said, I am used to how the length now). Secondly, the stock grip doesn't absorb sweat very well, so I'd recommend adding some grip tape (the paddle comes with some!).

Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm) I just received this from my wife as a Christmas gift. I have gone on 3 rides ranging from 20-60 miles and this helmet is great. A few months ago I went into my favorite local bike shop asking about helmets because I seem to have an unusually large head......yea, a mellon head. Most of the helmets I've tried were too small, too heavy, straps ran weird and uncomfortable, or just plain SQUARE. The Lasor O2 fit like no other helmet I've ever tried. This summer I started useing a "halo" sweat band and I have no problem with the fit, even with my huge mellon head. The unique helmet features a "adjustment dial" that will fine tune the fit to your head with laser percision. This helmet is much lighter than my old Bell I used to wear. You might not notice this on a 10-20 mile ride but if you ride any longer distances you will feel it. During the summer months, I live in Michigan, I try to do one century a month and ...BOY, I can hardly wait to do my first one this year. Another very important feature about this helmet is ....IT LOOKS COOL!! Even my niehbor who likes to make fun of cyclists because of there "pointy hats" said this one looks cool.

Don't look at another helmet. This is the best I've EVER worn. If you cycle a lot, don't hesitate. It's a bit more money but for the serious cyclist it's worth every penny. I try to ride at least 100 mile a week during the good months. If you ride simply with a family or short distances you might want to concider a cheaper model.....unless you have a big fat mellon head like me.

M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length I collect knives and hawks. There are two ways that I judge the effectiveness of any sharp tool. Number One is how it stacks up to a good machete. At this point if I could only take one blade into the wilderness, it would be a high quality machete. It has reach and a long cutting surface, is fundamental in design, and can create a large protected area around the user. In addition it cuts through things easily and doesn't typically get hung up in/on the target, unlike other implements. Number Two is judging how I would feel if I were threatened with the tool. It does look wicked, it has two effective blades, it comes sharp(!), can be swung in any direction, and is well built. It's inherent light weight will allow a lot of use before arm fatigue sets in, but it does have some negatives.

On the con side, it is short and its lightness doesn't make it feel substantial in my hand. The cutting surface is much smaller than that of a good machete and of course you can't really stab with it. It is a swinging tool that will allow an experienced fighter to step inside of the swing. Although I haven't tested it, it's hard for me to believe that it can stand up to the abuse that a large man can generate. The M48 probably wouldn't last long against a hard target (breaching doors or cutting wood or metal) but it should prove to be easy to carry and extremely effective against a soft target. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit with it. The best part of the M48 is the value. It is simply one of the most cost effective blades that I have ever bought. And darn, it just looks and feels cool!
text_fidelity_b: M48 Tactical Tomahawk Military Axe - Green/Black with Compass & Sheath | 3 ⅞” Cast Stainless Steel Axe | Piercing Spike | Nylon Cord Wrapped Fiberglass Handle | Camping and Tactical Gear | 15” Length

Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag This set includes:
- Six (6) all weather colored balls of one color of each (red, yellow, orange, blue, green, and black).
- Nine (9) all weather plastic coated metal wickets.
- Six (6) solid wood mallets with wooden handles (30.75 inches assembled) --one for each color. They have double metal locking joints and assembly is required each time.
- Two (2) 24" wooden stakes with colored lines that match the colors of the balls and mallet handles. NOTE that I received four (4) wooden stakes in my package (see picture).
- One carry case.
- One paltry instruction sheet.

I had always wanted to play croquet and this is my first set. When I first opened the package, I was really impressed and considered this five stars for the price since it contains everything needed to play. In order to store all the items in the carry case, the set must be disassembled each time after play. What I mean by this is that the wooden handles have to be screwed and unscrewed from the mallet head. Since I live in a condo, I cannot leave this set assembled after playing as I have no garage to store this in and I have to remove the wickets from the complex's lawn when done with the game.

After watching some how-to videos, my boyfriend and I played this. We had a lot of fun as it is a cross between golf and bocce ball to me.

It was during play that we noticed a problem with this set. The biggest issue is that each wood mallet with its associated handle kept loosening up no matter how hard we tightened it. Several times we had to re-tighten the mallets. Also, after our game was over, we noticed that the plastic coating on the wickets was chipping off on the bottom and exposing the metal and this was the first time we used the set. I suppose this is to be expected, however..

Overall, we enjoyed this game and the set seems to be good quality with the exception of the mallet head and its associated handle loosening up. It is for this reason only I rate this 3.4 stars. A really professional set would be more than double the price of this one. If I were in the market for a higher end set, I would look into this [[ASIN:B073YFZY9M Amish-made croquet set]].

OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12" This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.
text_fidelity_b: OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12"

text_fidelity_a: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock Great lock for securing secondary components like seat and front wheel on your bike.  I live in Baltimore where bike theft is an issue, but not as bad as it is in bigger cities.  The general recommendations are U-Lock your frame and rear wheel first, then secure the front wheel and seat with something like a cable or chain lock.  I needed this longer length chain to secure my seat, and I use the shorter Abus steel chain lock to secure my front wheel to the frame.  This may be a little bit of overkill, but it is not unusual in Baltimore to see locked up bikes with the front wheel missing, and I overheard a woman in my LBS who was coming in to buy a new seat because hers had just been stolen.  These things can/do happen, and the harder you make it for thieves, the more likely the thieves are to pass you by for an easier target.  Seats and quick-release wheels are easy to steal when left unsecured, and they are expensive to replace.  A cable lock costs about as much, but is significantly easier to defeat than these chain locks.  I like these Abus locks (this one and the shorter one) because they are a small investment for a lot of peace of mind.
text_fidelity_b: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock

text_fidelity_a:
Gonex Hand Crank Collapsible Outdoor LED Camping Lantern USB Rechargeable Mini Flashlight Hiking Torch light lamp Camp lanterns serve a couple of useful purposes. They can help light an area when outdoors (and camping) and they can be used as an emergency light source when there is need for extra light (such as during a power outage). Battery-powered lanterns offer more convenience and do not require liquid fuels. This particular lantern is especially suited for emergencies as it has a rechargeable power supply and it also has a hand-crank for getting short bursts of emergency power when it is otherwise depleted.

This is a small lantern that is a little smaller in diameter than a typical coaster. It is bright orange which will make it easy to find, even on a cluttered desk in the daylight. It is a collapsible unit and when collapsed (as it comes in the package) it is less than 2” thick and when expanded is about 5” tall.

It has two brightness modes, one being somewhat bright and the other being very bright. On the bottom of this lantern is a lens that sits over the internal LED and when the lantern is expanded the lens lets through a well-diffused and gentle light that illuminates a wide area. When collapsed the light coming from the lens is much more concentrated and is bright and defined enough to serve as a flashlight.

The power source for this lantern is an internal rechargeable battery. This can be charged with the included cable, but it is not a USB cable and instead uses a round plug. This is the one criticism I have of this lantern – don’t lose that cable. But…in addition to the cable the lantern includes a crank mechanism that can deliver some emergency power to the battery when needed, requiring a little manual effort. Unless you want to crank for a long, long time, do not expect the crank to charge this lantern up all the way or even close to it. It’s there for emergencies, not a primary charging source.

The unit is fairly rugged and weatherproof. It is sealed up nicely and should hold up well in adverse weather like light rain. I would not try to submerge it but I suspect it would survive if dropped in water briefly.

I like this lantern and I can see the possibilities with it. It’s a great little emergency light and it can work as a flashlight or a lantern. It’s small and it packs well. Just don’t lose the charging cable.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Gonex Hand Crank Collapsible Outdoor LED Camping Lantern USB Rechargeable Mini Flashlight Hiking Torch light lamp

Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1296 cubic inches
18” x 12” x 6”
7 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 6 1/2” of bottles
Straps 2 1/2” wide
This pack has 4 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a zippered compartment that extends the entire length of the pack. In the front at the top is a small zippered pocket. In the front on the bottom is another small zippered pocket. This is where the pack is stored when folded.
Pros:
- Very easy to adjust shoulder straps
- Straps are mesh on one side and fabric on the other side. These reinforced straps feel soft and pliable
- Pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying pack
- Large open at top pocket inside the pack against the back
- 4 main compartments rather than the typical 3.
Cons:
- Thinner material than a standard backpack.
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- No small zippered pocket inside the pack.

This was a larger, lightweight, foldable daypack that met my needs, so I ordered it in a different color.

text_fidelity_a:
Synergee Farmer Walk Straps. Farmer Carry Style Straps for Loaded Carries. Sold in Pairs, 400lbs Capacity. Full Body, Functional Exercise Equipment My wife and I are not professional weight lifters and do our own stuff at home. We like to have a variety of ways to workout and we've talked about a farmer's carry before. I had the chance to grab these Synergee Farmer Walk Straps and we decided to give it a shot. For us - total amateurs - this seems like a good set up. We did a little research and know there are those who swear by things that are more bar-like, but for us at this point, these have what we need and are good for us.

The Synergee Farmer Walk Straps have a rubber handle with a decent grip to it. I've carried them with and without my workout gloves and it was fine. The materials seem to be solid and strong, well constructed, and that they'll give us longevity. I can't remember the weight limits, but we're well within I'm sure. The biggest thing for us will be getting the straps attached and lockdown well enough. You run the strap through the hole(s) on the weight you are using - we are starting with 1 X 25lbs each. Then lock it off in the buckle and wrap the rest around itself and out of the way. It's not as easy as it seemed it would be - we need practice - but it was by no means dangerous and did keep the strap out of the way and the weight secure. We'll get better. Then carrying the weight was fine - easy. We are slightly different heights, but we both felt comfortable with our first try length on the strap. That said, the one thing that IS a CON: deciding HOW LONG the strap and weight placement should be without testing and retesting. We ended up guessing and it seemed fine, nothing was hurt and hit when carrying, but it was not the easiest nor most efficient way of going about it. But it's no big deal at this point. If we get to a larger load point that exceeds that we think the straps can do - say more than 2 X 25 lbs weights that would then be swinging next to our leg, we'll maybe go for something else. We're open to seeing how this plays out. ** The last photo is me holding up the strap and handle to show the length of the strap, but not sure it shows it well enough.

So, for a beginner, we feel like this Synergee Farmer Walk Straps gets us going and on a good path, but for longer term, yes, we expect we'll outgrown these and go for something more "professional." Pros:
1. Packs down small and does not take up much room in a backpack.
2. Fairly light
3. Fly can be rolled up to allow for maximum airflow when the weather permits.
Cons:
1. Not free standing. Must be staked down.
2. Fly is not removable.
3. No vestibule.
4. Must crawl in/out from the front. Can be hard to keep from getting wet/dirty if there was a storm/rain the night before.

Overall, if you are looking for a bivy style tent, this probably is what you want. Unless you want an ultra-light, which this is not.

Would be really good for motorcycle or bike camping. Not really for backpacking, as the weight is comparable to a good 2 person tent!
If I were going to carry a 3lb+ tent, I would get one with enough room to sit up in and that has a vestibule. Plenty of those tents out there in the 3lb range.

Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown

Body Bar Power & Grace DVD This workout uses both a body bar and the gliding disks. Instructor Mindy Mylrea is joined by Keli Roberts, who modifies some of the exercises, and Violet Zaki, who increases the intensity.

Mylrea starts with a long (about 7 minutes) warm-up. During the warm-up, you are just holding the body bar and not really using it for resistance. In addition, she does not step on the disks until about halfway through the warm-up; at that time, she incorporates added moves such as twists plus side and back lunges.

For the standing portion of the workout, Mylrea takes greater advantage of the body bar. The option is often to hold the bar at the chest, on the shoulders, or overhead while performing classic strength moves such as side and front lunges, curtsey lunges, and deadlifts. The standing segment ends with push-up/plank work with the feet on the disks.

The floor work is shorter (18 minutes), but it continues to focus on the lower body with bridges and other moves targeting the hamstrings. Mylrea also includes abs work and a nice floor stretch (6 minutes), bringing in the entire workout right around 54 minutes.

I really enjoy Mylrea's original Gliding set, as I like mixing and matching from the 3 workouts on that DVD. For some reason, this workout didn't click as well with me, even though there aren't any major problems with the workout itself. One issue is that I do not have a body bar; substituting an unweighted stick and dumbbells worked okay, but this took some fun out of the workout. I also think that I have moved away from these type of cardio/strength circuit workouts now that I have discovered kettlebells.

For those who own both a body bar and gliding disks, however, I would recommend this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: Body Bar Power & Grace DVD

Levi's Men's 2-Horse Graphic Tee I decided to rate this 4-stars DESPITE getting the wrong “version” which would’ve dropped it to 3-stars.

I had requested the “(New) Dress Blues” version (red print on dark blue); I ended up with the “: (New) Mineral Black” (white print on black). And, honestly? I LOVE the version I got instead. Definitely more clear and bold.

Definitely comfy too.

So, if I like the print style and the comfort, why 4-stars?

THE FIT.

I’m a plus-size girl, so I tend to wear bigger clothes. And, for a gal that wears a 3XL? This fits my frame 100% perfectly. No slouch, no overages, nothing “boxy”.

Why is that a problem?

This is a MEN’s PLUS-SIZE. It shouldn’t FIT like a LADIES 3XL. I know because when I’d buy “mens” (or unisex) t-shirts at souvenir places or the racetracks – the 3XL versions would always be BIGGER than the women’s versions. Also, the “cut” would be more “boxy” for the lack of a better term.

This had a more “ladies” cut/style to it.

It is also shorter than the usual MENS style. This fit rather “short” for a guy, but perfect on my LADIES’ body – almost like it was for a girl.

It had ALL the LEVIs tags – the country/care tag, price tag, side tag, and even the “screen print” neck tag. So, definitely a genuine article.

Perhaps it was a “unicorn” (rare) shirt or how the t-shirt are being designed.

If you’re a BIGGER guy and need a long, boxy, big tee – I wouldn’t recommend this.

If you’re a bigger gal that wants a well-fit, slim, and shorter tee – I’d definitely get this.
text_fidelity_b: Levi's Men's 2-Horse Graphic Tee

text_fidelity_a:
bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1071 cubic inches
17” x 10.5” x 6”
6 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 5 1/2” of bottles
Straps 3” wide
Hard to adjust shoulder straps, especially to loosen them
Straps feel soft and pliable
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a small zippered pocket. In the front is a mesh compartment which is held closed by a strap and buckle. I did not like having a mesh compartment.
Pros:
- Lightweight
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying it
- Side pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Medium sized zippered pouch inside the large compartment – this is where the pack is stored when folded
- Large pocket inside on the back of the large compartment
- 1 extra loop on outside bottom of pack.
- Extra side support straps
Cons:
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- Some padding on the back panel
- Shoulder straps were several layers of mesh but NOT fortified with the nylon fabric
- Things stored in front mesh compartment would get dirtier and wetter than in a pack with a zippered fabric covered compartment.

I returned this pack. It was a nice foldable pack, but I didn't like the mesh pocket in the front.
text_fidelity_b: bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight

text_fidelity_a:
REDCAMP Nylon Compression Stuff Sack, 10L/17L/27L/40L Lightweight Sleeping Bag Compression Sack Great for Backpacking, Hiking and Camping,Blue/Yellow/Army Green/Black I did read the measurements - I was cutting it close. I have a surplus sleep system bivy cover and green inner bag I use for cooler weather camp trips. The compression bag that normally comes with it is a bit big for just these two components, so I wanted one a little smaller so I could stuff it into one of the side bags of the motorcycle. I got the small size, the medium was bigger than what I could use. The small was very slender, I had to unroll my sleeping bag, and roll it up from the head down and fold it over in half to fit in this compression sack. I'm glad this bag comes with straps on the sides, I would be afraid the sack might split from the pressure of this sleeping bag. I might update this after the trip is over and I stuff the bag back into this compression sack. Maybe even take a picture with it in the side pannier for size comparison. For size - imagine this; you cannot fit a regular size coffee can over the opening of this sack and have enough fabric to pull over.

Update: After my journey out, and my journey back. For a sleeping bag this size; you have to roll it a few different ways until it works. Fold it in half until its bag width, then roll it as tight as you can. Proof is in the pudding, the bag fits just perfect and still fits into my side bag on the motorcycle. Not really sure what to put into the little pocket on top, maybe an extra pillow cover? Or small flashlight. Hope this picture helps someone decide what they need. I would buy again for other things I need to compress down.
text_fidelity_b: REDCAMP Nylon Compression Stuff Sack, 10L/17L/27L/40L Lightweight Sleeping Bag Compression Sack Great for Backpacking, Hiking and Camping,Blue/Yellow/Army Green/Black

Are you joists spaced far enough apart so that you can actually fit a drill w/ bit in between them to make the holes?

Turns out mine weren't, or rather, that almost all of them weren't, except for one awkwardly overspaced gap right up against a dividing wall that almost had enough to room to squeeze the drill in there and make holes. Anyway, after a few hours of cursing and intermittently giving up I finally got the thing up and it feels great. The handles are a good distance and offer many positions for hands to do chin/pull -ups. My joists are standard 2 in thick and about 10 in deep, I have the screws mounted about 4 inches up and so far it seems very sturdy. Hopefully nothing breaks, but thus far my expectations are high.

text_fidelity_a: Epiphany Outdoor Gear Pocket Bellows - Weatherproof Collapsible Fire Bellowing Tool for Starting Fire- an Essential Camping Gear After years of blowing at camp fires through pursed lips and getting a face and eyes and lungs full of smoke, I saw a product demonstrated on a Bush Craft video.  It was only available in Europe...  Then I found this on Amazon.  It is stainless steel so it is not light weight for its (small) size.  Its value is in its function and in its collapsiblity.  From a collapsed state of just under 4 inches, it extends to 19 inches,  The larger (.5 inches, diameter) end is placed in the mouth and the narrow end concentrates  oxygenated air from your lungs to a focused stream at the narrow end. Once an initial spark or flame has begun to produce an ember, combustion can be sped up by directing more air precisely at the ember.  That sure beats watching helplessly while the initial spark fails to catch and fades to nothing.  On a dry day with dry, finely processed wood, this might not be needed...but on a cold, damp day with wood that is a bit damp, this makes all the difference between fire and failure.  At first, this device will be stiff to open and close but a little lubricant will help.  Opened up, the rod is sturdy and should last for a good many fires.
text_fidelity_b: Epiphany Outdoor Gear Pocket Bellows - Weatherproof Collapsible Fire Bellowing Tool for Starting Fire- an Essential Camping Gear

This is made in China of 90% polyester and10% polyamide. It should not be washed in water above 30 degrees Celsius (86 degrees Fahrenheit) and should never be put in the dryer, ironed, dry cleaned, or bleached.

The material does not feel like the microfiber dusty clothes I have come to know which is fuzzy and catches a lot of lint. Instead, this towel is super soft and slinky and thin. It is also large as can be seen when I laid it across the foot of my king-sized bed. The material repels sand, which is great. However, this is not super absorbent in my opinion. I do not like drying myself with this at all. It does absorb water some but it does not feel right against the skin as a beach towel. I felt like I was drying myself with a slinky scarf.

Nevertheless, I love the design and functionality of this towel. Unfortunately, once the towel is removed from its carrier, the carrier becomes useless. I tried to put the towel back into its carrier after it was dry and it was impossible. Eventually, the carrier just ripped (see photo).

In summary, I consider this more of a thin beach cloth or mat than a towel. I love that it repels sand, feels great against the skin, is lightweight, and large. I love the idea of a carry case but the case is way too small that it becomes useless. I do love the elastic on the towel which allows me to keep it tightly rolled. However, I would never use this like a beach towel to dry myself off. It can, however, be used a little like a wrap on the lower half of the body or slightly over the shoulders. The current price of $20.89 ($21.99 minus 5%) is a little pricey for this. This gets 3.5 stars from me rounded up to 4 stars.

The video was useless as to how to install the handlebars, it only covered brakes and had only cheesy music, no actual verbal instructions so you had to kind of guess what the guy was doing. The guy in the video was using tools that were not included nor listed as needed for the job. The videographer also did not zoom in when he should have to show the small details. It took us 10 times longer than it should have to get this thing put together because the directions suck so bad. It's too bad because I would have given this 5 stars if there were even halfway decent instructions. It is a nice scooter especially for the price but be prepared to get extremely frustrated with the assembly.

text_fidelity_a:
NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board, Upgrade Version 10′ 6″ Paddle Board with Free Premium SUP Accessories & Backpack,10L Dry Bag, Phone Pouch, Shoulder Strap. So far this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is pretty darn good and we think it’ll turn out to be a great SUP for us. My wife and I have wanted our own SUPs for awhile, but we have no where to store a regular SUP and had considered blow up versions. When I had a chance to get this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board I took it. Unfortunately for us, it’s taken a longer than desired time to get a chance to try them - and due to weather (storms, hurricanes) and my recovery from surgery, we’ve been unable to get onto the water. So at this point we are only able to review based on the specific SUP and it’s kit - I will update when if need be when we get it on the water. In the mean time, this is a nice set up and we think it’s gonna be a great SUP. The kit is excellent, with items such as a dry bag for your pone included. There is a patch kit. Also a carrying bag. The carrying bag is a little... weird. The bag sets high - the actual straps are set low on the bag so the top of the bag is higher - at the head or perhaps above depending on your size. But it works on. My wife wore it for the pictures and said it was comfortable, but that it set “weird,” and she felt she could wear it from the car to wherever we were to launch, comfortably. But, I did have to help her get it on and off due to the placement of the straps.

Pumping the SUP: It took us a bit to figure this process out, but once we had it, it went fine. The instruction book is pretty tiny writing, so we took a picture and adjusted it. We can also keep the instructions with on our phones for when we’re out. The tube was easy to insert - took a few times popping out to get it to stay on - there is a way to adjust the pump as it gets harder to pump and we did use it. My wife pumped for awhile, then I did. It IS a bit tough to do. NOT the actual pumping, but the amount of time and it does get harder - adjust the dial - but we only got as high as the 8 PSI not to the 15 they recommend. As we get back into shape following being off workouts for awhile, we’ll get better at it, but between us - for this test run - we were only able to hit that 8 and we had to give up. It FELT fine at this level, but WOW....! We WILL TRY to get to that 15, but ... WOW! My wife stood on it and it felt great, but she said she sees how the 15 would be “better,” yet... will we ever be able to get that high. There are two blades on the bottom - and you add the fin - they are in a holder to protect them when it’s down.

Deflating was really easy. And it took only minutes. This SUP has you use the pump to help clear out the final air and that worked great. The prong you push in the air hole is really easy to use and my wife was thrilled with it.

Overall we are impressed with this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and look forward to FINALLY being able to use it on the water - when it’s safe. It comes with a break-apart paddle. We have not used it nor put it together, but we did get ourselves another paddle - we think it’s lighter. We’ll keep them both and take both with. It’s a practice we were taught - to have a backup. But right now I can’t speak to how good theirs is. But we are impressed. at this point, we can’t wait to get out there on this NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board!
text_fidelity_b: NACATIN Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board, Upgrade Version 10′ 6″ Paddle Board with Free Premium SUP Accessories & Backpack,10L Dry Bag, Phone Pouch, Shoulder Strap.

text_fidelity_a:
H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

text_fidelity_a:
Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps… For under 100 bucks shipped you get everything you need to get out on the water minus life vests. The skeg has been improved as it now has a new locking mechanism and silhouette. The 86" paddles are well made for the price, nicely curved, have an adjustable paddle angle and float (as we found out accidentally) so paddle leashes are recommend. The boat is stable when inflated properly using the pressure gauge "measuring strip" and did not rock too bad when standing up in the aft position with an adult seated up front. The boat has a drain plug in the stern which has to be closed as mine was shipped in the open position. The 30 gauge PVC (Vinyl) has a nylon like backing and appears to be rugged enough for large lakes and mild moving waters. Not sure I would personally use this on class III+ water but some reviewer's have reported their own success stories. It tracks well on flat water with the skeg and okay with a peaceful river current without. Seats are more comfortable than I originally imagined when purchasing. Watch out for over inflation as we pumped her up at 64° and by the afternoon the temp had increased to 74° which caused the inflation gauge to read 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) higher due to air expansion. Over all I am impressed for the cost of purchase. It comes with one 3"x3" self adhesive patch similar to "Tear-Aid type B" (looks like a square piece of yellow card stock) and two 2" clear patches that require you to use your own PVC cement. The pump tube can be stored inside the pump itself by unscrewing the end and coiling it around the pump shaft. It packs up into a Blackhawk tactical bag that I have as the Intex bag was uncomfortable to carry since it didn't have a shoulder strap. The boat is 22.2 lbs without the seats, 25.8 lbs with both seats not including other accessories. Takes about 10 minutes to setup with the included air pump or 5 minutes with the 12v Intex pump (which has deflate mode too!!!).

Things to remember include closing the drain plug and monitoring inflation to prevent over inflation related seam tears. If you know the temp will increase throughout the day by 5-10° i would recommend under inflating by 5-10% (0.5-1 cm) on the inflation gauge which is approximately 10 cm long when fully inflated.
text_fidelity_b: Explorer K2 Kayak, 2-Person Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars, Manual and Electric Pumps…

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent This arrived today and I was very anxious to try to set it up. We camped a lot when I was a child and setting up the tent always involved a lot of cussing on someone's part. This wasn't too different an experience in some ways.

Pros:

Fairly easy to set up the first time out of the box. I did it by myself.
Lightweight enough for a woman to carry
Large floor space and tall enough for a 6' 2" man to stand up in.
Lots of vents and windows
Nice rainfly

Cons:
Impossible directions. You don't need them too much to get set up, but you need some guidance to get the tent down and back in the bag. It took 3 tries to finally get it in there
The center beam on the top that keeps the tent stretched out, did not lock in place for us. I don't know if this is a defect or just poor design
Because of the lightweight nature of this, the floor and walls are very thin material. The floor reminds me of one of those really cheap plastic tarps that you can get.
The metal stakes that are used to hold in the feet of the poles bend very easily if you hit a rock or an obstacle.
Not very secure when set up. I think this would need some serious tent stakes to hold it down in any kind of wind. It was windy here today and I'm not sure this would have stayed together too long.
The zippers are not going to take much use, in fact the whole thing might be good for one season of regular camping and use/abuse.

All in all, I was hoping for better. At least something that kids visiting us could use. Maybe with a little tweaking we can get it stable.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Camping Instant Signal Mountain Tent

GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing I selected this luminous key ring as an aid to attaching to my camera bag and being visible at night. I wasn’t exactly sure what to expect and I had some serious doubts about the effectiveness of this product. It turns out that it’s better than I had hoped and it works well.

The concept is very simple: expose it to bright light for a little while and it will glow in the dark for a longer while. The claim is that it will glow for up to 10 hours; I have not verified that it will last that long, but it does go for a long time, long enough in most situations that it will continue to glow long after sunset. This is really all I can ask.

The vial appears to be filled with some sort of phosphorous-coated granules. As a first test I exposed them to the bright light of an LED flashlight for about 30 seconds, and the vial glowed for several minutes afterward. It wasn’t all that bright, but I didn’t give it long to “charge” either. It was enough as a proof of concept though. It lasts longer under extended exposure to bright light such as direct sunlight.

The extra clips that come with the vial are useful for attaching it to other things without using the ring. One of the attachments is actually the same thing as a pen clip, which is useful for clipping to a tent flap, umbrella or other fabric surface.

Especially when considering the cost, this is really an easy product to recommend if you need a luminous marker. It really does work for a long while, it’s very easy to see and it is versatile.
text_fidelity_b: GEAR AID Ni Glo, 2” Glowing Keychain for Camping, Scuba and Night Fishing

text_fidelity_a:
Walker's Razor Slim The things I was curious about before buying these:
A) How they sound.
B) How they feel.
C) Compared to Howard Leights by Honeywell as well as the BT edition of the Walker Razor.

I have not tested the Noise Cancellation yet but provided it works as it should I wanted to get out my review in case anyone wondered what I did. My hand's on impressions have been fully positive.
If you get these and wonder how to open the package: I just bent the package in half. This caused the cardboard to split open and the plastic clamshell is not sealed - it is 2 parts and the headphones came out super simple.

How do they sound? (I own Sennheiser HD600 compared to those:)
A)Surprisingly good. Not audiophile but not bad.
B)Bass is light. Not much bass from these. Bass seems purposely reserved, truth be told probably neutral.
C)Slight emphasis on mid-range. But not annoying in any frequency.
D)Highs are present but not pristine.
E)Overall, they sound good for a $43 set of headphones that do so much more. I am pleased with it. I can listen without irritation.

How do they feel?
A) A little tight on my medium-sized head but the muffs are plushy and do a good job of distributing the clamp pressure.
B) I can't imagine wearing these for much more than an hour at a time but it might be ok for longer but probably no one will actually want to.
C) Headband doesn't rub my scalp.
D) No hair pulling or "pinchy parts".
E) The hinges that hold the muffs look thin but they work (so far). Durability could be a concern.
F) The hinges are adjustable. I collapsed then down about 2/5ths of the way so they could possibly fit larger heads but wider heads may have more clamp pressure?
G) Again, the clamp pressure is pretty tight. I am surprised how tight they are. But they stay on the head when moving my head which is good. It is a good thing they are tight but it could cause them to fatigue your head after a while. Be aware they are pretty tight on the head but I don't believe it will be a deal-breaker.

How is the enhanced hearing:
A) Fairly natural. I can rather accurately distinguish sounds.
B) I never knew what a bee flying sounded like other than Bumblebees right in my ear. I heard the bee and I will learn that sound but I wouldn't have known what it was had I not seen the bee and heard the sound.
C) You will discover new sounds you haven't heard before.
D) Unfortunately, the sound is mono-sounding like everyone has said. Determining the origin or placement of noises does not work out so well.
E) I questioned whether to get these or the Howard Leight by Honeywell. I decided to try these first after listening to YouTube videos. I have read reviews that say the "Howard's" better determine which direction noises come from but some videos said they do not do it better enough to choose them over these.
F) These are supposedly more comfortable than the Howard Leights.
G) They are cheaper and look better IMO than the Howard Leights.
H) I might buy the Howard Leights just to see if the sound placement is better because I think that would be a big deal but from what I have read and heard the hype may or may not be all it is cracked up to be. The reviewers mostly chose these over the Howard Leight.

Overall, I am impressed that these are only $43.
Be sure to get a 3.5mm to 3.5mm male to male wire to use them for music.
I wanted to get the Bluetooth version but after reading how much problems people were having with the BT dropping or not working, I decided to get the wired version.
The BT version has 4 mics which, on paper, seems would give better awareness of surroundings but from things I heard it didn't quite work as well in RL as it seems it would. I still would like to try those because it would be worth the money to me if they worked like they should but if they didn't I knew I would still be getting these.
text_fidelity_b: Walker's Razor Slim

text_fidelity_a:
KENAI 65 Cooler | 65 qt Ice Chest Durable Rotomolded Insulated | Made in USA | Warranty for Life | for Beach Boat Camping Fishing Hunting | K65 UPDATE AFTER VACATION;
the best thing about this cooler for longer trips, its dry ice ready. We spent 15$ on dry ice, used the divider (frozen) and our ice didnt start to melt until day 6 on the way home. This cooler worked as well as the Yeti for 3x less money. I'm so happy and proud of my cooler I use it almost everyday. Our beach trip was a total success and we saved 6$ a day on ice at the minimum. Perfect cooler for everyday use, beach, river, lake and just about any time you need. Plenty of room and easy to clean. A must buy

Update, 1st use breakdown.

Did NOT precool cooler, Used Grizzly Brand ice divider (owns Kenia coolers), and my cans were pre chilled in fridge.
I only used 1 half of my cooler using the frozen divider. The other half stayed empty.

10lbs ice 1st day ( rd side ice machine which isnt the best ice and melts quick) after 36 hrs I only had around 2 cups of water because the divider was refreezing the water as it melted against the divider and along the bottom of cooler.
Day 3 I added 20lbs of frozen ice. Still only half of cooler. Didnt have but a quart or so of melt off by this point and divider was half melted. The ice last 2 more days before I drained 1.25 to 1.5 gallons of water from cooler and had maybe 7 lbs of lightly frozen ice left.

This cooler is awesome from my use and my experience with using it. Today I've added 20lbs of ice NO divider and using entire cooler and I still only have a cup of water. Temp is 80 degrees constantly and 15 hrs have gone by already. This is still the rd side machine ice, as I said before in a normal cooler 20lbs will melt within 20 hrs for sure by next morning it's all water. With the Kenia cooler I have easily doubled my ice time if not almost tripling it. And I'm not freezing the ice in a freezer before use. If you freeze this crap ice before use, it can last 4 or so days. If u freeze ice in deep freezer I'm sure it will last even longer because of the - temps with deep freezer.

Well worth the money spent and saved vs a 600$ equivalent yeti. This cooler will pay for it self over 40 total days, 5$ or more per bag ice, 1 bag per day 200$... paid for that quick. At least with my old coolers this is what I was having to do, either 6$ bag ice from store or 2 rd side bags @4$ per day. Every day and during our Southern 100 degree days I was having to do this twice a day. So by far this cooler out last most on market.

Now I added 20 lbs of frozen freezer ice to that 10lbs, didnt drain the water. The ice lasted 4 days. I hope this helps someone make the right choice for the money.
We have a beach trip planned in few months and another updated test results will come after that trip. That test will be outside in middle summer outside 16+ hrs a day in direct sunlight. Will update after words to tell the world.

Look 5 stars even though ITS LOOKS TO BE USED!!
yes it is scratched on top and scuffed on side and bottom and it does not smell like a factory cooler smells when purchased. With the way its wrapped and boxed this shouldnt happen if it was brand new. I could be wrong and issues arise from warehouse worshipping problems. But it seems to be a returned item that has been used at least once.

Overall this cooler is huge, thick, and very sturdy! Cheaper by almost 70% from yeti brand. I'm very pleased with purchase.
The color is absolutely vibrant and eye catching. I love the stapdown handles and the thick rubber feet on bottom.
The inside is just amazing you can tell it will hold heat or cold very easily.

I wish there were more accessories available with the 65 quart coolers.. that's my only big issue besides the used look.
I bought a rack from yeti hoping to bend it the .1 inch to fit (judging by measurements provide by companies). I have also bought the 5lbs freezer divider so we can keep usable ice seperate from used ice with the dry ice.

Camping trip in next few weeks will give a good idea of how well this cooler cools. Will update at that time and let everyone know how this cooler works in real world settings.

As I have had time to use and play with these 5 different Joola Ping Pong paddles, I must say that they are all incredible compared to any other Ping Pong paddle I have ever used. The quality and performance far exceeds my previous experiences.

Each of these paddles have been designed for a specific purpose which include speed, spin and control. Now not being a professional, I can not “honestly” say that I notice the difference between any of these five different paddles, in any of the different design aspects while using them. However, I can honestly say that visually I can tell the difference by the different rubber padding (sandwiched between the inner and outer rubber) used in each. Some have a slightly different thickness, weight, color and I assume different “springiness”. With that said, each and every one of them have performed absolutely stellar in every way for my, and my family’s play style. Personally they all have incredible spin, speed and control capabilities. They are all built with beautiful build quality, and designed with comfort and balance in mind. I especially love the resin looking inlaid logo at the end of the handles. I realise that it doesn’t make a performance difference but it just ads to the overall beauty and gives each paddle a quality looking finish.

Overall I feel quite privileged to have had the opportunity to use and experience the Joola brand and share my opinions, though I feel absolutely unqualified to have done so. Just know that if you have never used or played with a “quality” Ping Pong paddle, you are truly missing out, and this Joola brand will be the only brand I choose from here on out! The quality is impeccable!!

text_fidelity_a: SABRE Personal Safety Kit With Pepper Spray and Personal Alarm, 25 Bursts, Intuitive Finger Grip, 120dB Alarm, Audible Up To 1,280-Feet (390-Meters) I have never used any type of pepper spray or personal safety items. I thought it might give some peace of mind during some situations. The items are two separate devices, so there are two things to keep track of. Ideally, it would be great if they were combined somehow into one device. Both items have a key chain attachment so you can keep it with your keys. I have put them on a lanyard instead though, for fear of accidently setting them off. I keep the lanyard inside the outer pocket of my purse. I can also wear the lanyard around my neck if desired. I was afraid to test these items, but I did. To activate the alarm, you pull the pin with the key chain. Once it's removed, a loud, piercing sound is made. It frightened the cats immediately! It wasn't too loud that it hurts your ears. It kind of reminded me of a car alarm sound. The alarm stops when you reinsert the pin and click it in place.  My husband and I tested the pepper spray outside. It was a windy day, so we made sure that we didn't spray it against the wind. A reddish orange stream of pepper spray was dispensed. The description of the product says it goes about 10 feet. We didn't measure it, but that seems pretty close to what we got. I like that you get about 25 sprays from it. I did get some on my finger. It dripped down from the dispenser. I immediately wiped my hand on the grass, then went inside and washed it thoroughly.  I was able to get it off because it didn't burn or sting. It doesn't have much of a smell. Hopefully, I won't have to use these! There is an expiration date on the pepper spray which is good to know.
